final_assessment:
Resume session on clean-up-review-cycle, opened immediately after rc04d archived. One ratification, one ruling clarification, one deliberate non-prompt.

RATIFICATION. rc04d-override-vocabulary is COMPLETE, ratified 2026-09-22 by Sal, written into its slot. Ratified on measurement re-run against the post-archive tree rather than on the archive's own report: exit (1) greps ZERO across the three capabilities, exit (2) shows src/ untouched with 2238/2238 green, exit (3) reads 6 capabilities down to 3. The split arithmetic closes exactly — gate_overridden spanned 14 requirements across 6 capabilities, rc04d took 5 across 3, and rc04c now inherits a MEASURED 9 across 3 (run-summary-emit 4, archive-modifications 4, emit-composition 1), the figure its charter has claimed since the split and which is now verified rather than asserted. Both halves sit AT R-crc-1's ceiling, which is what R-crc-9's third preventive application existed to produce.

THE RULING WORK, and it is the part that mattered. Ratifying required deciding what rc04d's mid-cadence exit-(2) change actually WAS, and the flattering answer was available: call it an R-crc-12 revision and the stage looks like it exercised a ratified escape. It was not one. R-crc-12 licenses revision only when the SHIPPED MECHANISM changed the criterion's meaning, and rc04d — a pure-vocabulary stage — shipped no mechanism at all. The criterion was measurable throughout; what was defective was the COMMAND written to measure it, an unscoped git diff standing in for a change-scoped claim. So the criterion graded, and it graded MET. Recorded as R-crc-12's third case precisely because that ruling says of itself that it is easy to abuse, and because 'I fixed the measuring tool' and 'the criterion changed meaning' produce the same diff in a task file while meaning opposite things. The corollary the stage earned the hard way: rc04d's task had tightened its bar from src/ to src/ AND test/ without the charter ever saying so, and it was the unratified half that appeared to fail — so a task may not silently narrow the bar its stage is graded against.

THE NON-PROMPT. rc03a-blind-prompt remains quiescent-awaiting-ratification and was NOT re-prompted: its offer fired and was declined earlier the same day, and firing an identical declined prompt twice within one day is the nagging the body is told never to do. Stated in prose, slot left [ ], and noted in the log because Q-crc-11 is accumulating cost evidence and a SUPPRESSED firing is a different datum from an absent one.

Second consecutive session where a capture was appended INSIDE an existing ruling rather than promoted to a new one, both times to keep the ruling count at 13 and the src:rulings marker and sources-registry pin out of an uncommitted tree. Worth naming as a habit now rather than discovering it as a pattern later. Doc validates; sources clean at 13 rulings, 22 stages, 21 capabilities, schema 4. Not arc-done.
rulings_captured: R-crc-12 — THIRD CASE (added 2026-09-22, settled under R-crc-3): an INSTRUMENT CORRECTION is not a REVISION and must not be recorded as one. The ruling split two cases (mechanism changed the criterion's meaning → revise; stage missed the bar → MISS); rc04d hit a third, where the criterion was right and measurable and the command written to measure it measured something else. Its own distinguishing question answers YES, so the criterion grades — and it graded MET. Corollary: an exit criterion lives in the CHARTER; the command in a task is only its instrument, and a task may not silently narrow the bar its stage is graded against.
